prompt: Why does this lesson keep its failing tests in `evidence/` instead of marking them with `test.fail()` under `tests/`?

choices.text: It would count as a pass and lose its trace
choices.why: Right. `retain-on-failure` keeps evidence only when the outcome was not the declared one, and the run of lesson 3's file left no trace.

choices.text: `test.fail()` stops the test before the browser opens
choices.why: The marked test ran for six seconds and failed at its assertion; the annotation changes how the result is counted, not whether it runs.

choices.text: Playwright refuses `test.fail()` when a trace setting is given
choices.why: The run with `--trace retain-on-failure` accepted it and reported *2 passed*.

choices.text: Folders other than `tests/` run faster
choices.why: Where a test file lives changes which configuration finds it, not its speed.

prompt: In `evidence.config.js`, what does `...base.use` inside `use` protect?

choices.text: The `webServer` that starts the shop
choices.why: `webServer` sits outside `use`, and `...base` at the top already copies it.

choices.text: The `list` reporter
choices.why: The reporter is set at the top level of the file, and this one names `list` again itself.

choices.text: The `baseURL`, which a bare `use` would replace
choices.why: Right. A key written after the spread replaces the whole object it names, so the base's `use` has to be spread again inside it.

choices.text: The `testDir`
choices.why: `testDir` is not inside `use`, and this file changes it to `evidence` on purpose.

prompt: To film every test and delete the film of each one that passes, the configuration sets video: ' ___ ' .
Match each file a failing test left to the question it answers.

pairs.right: What the screen showed at the end
What the page held, as greppable text
What happened, in what order, and when

prompt: In the failing click's `error-context.md`, the Banana button carries `[active]`. Which story does that rule out?

choices.text: That the server counted the basket wrong
choices.why: The focus says nothing about the server; that story is ruled out later, by the trace showing no request at all.

choices.text: That the request to the basket went out and failed
choices.why: The error context holds no network at all; only the trace can say whether a request was made.

choices.text: That the page never drew the products
choices.why: True that it is ruled out, but by the eight list items, not by `[active]`.

choices.text: That the click missed the button
choices.why: Right. `[active]` marks the element with the focus, and the button got it by being clicked.

prompt: The failing click's screenshot shows eight cards and *Basket: 0 items*, and nothing looks wrong. What does that tell you?

choices.text: The failure comes from a flaky test, so it can safely be ignored this time
choices.why: A screenshot says nothing about how often a test fails, and this one fails on every run.

choices.text: The page drew everything; the defect is in how it got there
choices.why: Right. A missing element or a broken layout is ruled out, and the question moves to order and time, which only the trace holds.

choices.text: Screenshots are taken before the assertion runs
choices.why: `only-on-failure` takes the picture at the end, after the assertion gave up.

choices.text: The video holds the same frame and need not be kept
choices.why: Here the video would add little, but that is a judgement about this failure, not a rule about videos.

prompt: In the trace, `/slow/ssr.js` was requested at 2178.2 and took 1504.6 ms; the click started at 2191.6. How many milliseconds before the script arrived did the click happen?
hint: Arrival is the start plus the time it took.

prompt: Put what the failing click's trace recorded in the order it happened.
trap: The script was asked for before the click, which makes it tempting to think it arrived first; it took a second and a half.

prompt: In the search race's `0-trace.network`, the answer to `papaya` is the first line and the answer to `p` the last, although `p` was asked first. Why?

choices.text: Lines are written as responses finish
choices.why: Right. The file's order is arrival order, which is exactly the defect: the shortest query is the slowest to answer.

choices.text: The browser sorts requests by the length of the address
choices.why: Nothing sorts them; the order is the moment each one was finished.

choices.text: Playwright writes the network file backwards
choices.why: The requests for the page and its script come first in the same file, in the order they ended.

choices.text: The `type` action sent the keys in reverse
choices.why: The starts, in `_monotonicTime`, go from `p` to `papaya`; the keys were sent in order.

prompt: A test clicks Save and fails because a message never appears. Its trace shows the click, then `POST /api/save` answered `500`. Which story does that support?

choices.text: The click came before the page's script had attached a handler
choices.why: Then no request would have been sent at all, as in the shop's `/ssr`; here one was.

choices.text: The click missed the button
choices.why: A missed click causes no request; this one caused exactly the request Save makes.

choices.text: The server failed the request the click sent
choices.why: Right. The page did its part and the server answered with an error, so the report goes to whoever owns the server.

choices.text: The test's assertion is too impatient
choices.why: A longer wait would not turn a `500` into a saved record.

prompt: Why is `testInfo.attach` called in `afterEach` and not as the last line of the test?

choices.text: Attachments are only accepted from hooks
choices.why: A test can attach too; the issue is whether that line is reached.

choices.text: `afterEach` runs before the page closes, the test after
choices.why: The test body runs first; the order is the other way round, and the messages are already in the array either way.

choices.text: It keeps the attachment out of passing tests
choices.why: The hook runs for passing tests too and attaches their messages as well.

choices.text: A failed line stops the test, never its hooks
choices.why: Right. The test stopped at the failing `expect`, which is exactly when the messages are wanted.

prompt: The page event that fires for an error a script threw and nobody caught is called ___ .
The trace already holds the console error and the page error. What does attaching them add?

choices.text: Nothing; the attachment repeats the trace and can go
choices.why: It repeats the evidence, and puts it where it is read first: in the terminal, and in tests that kept no trace.

choices.text: The same evidence, where it is read first
choices.why: Right. Under `retain-on-failure` a passing test keeps no trace, and the `list` reporter prints a text attachment in place.

choices.text: It makes the test fail when the page throws
choices.why: Attaching only records; failing on an error is the extra `expect` the section shows.

choices.text: The time of each message
choices.why: The times are in the trace; the attachment in this lesson is plain text without them.

prompt: With `trace: 'on-first-retry'` and one retry, a test fails and then passes on its retry. What trace do you have?

choices.text: Only the retry's, the run that passed
choices.why: Right. That is this setting's blind spot: the run you need to see is the one it did not record.

choices.text: One of the failing first attempt
choices.why: The first attempt is never recorded under this setting; the capture's first folder had a screenshot and a video and no trace.

choices.text: None, because the test ended green and nothing failed in the end
choices.why: The retry is recorded whatever its outcome; that is what the setting means.

choices.text: Two, one for each attempt
choices.why: That would be `'on'` with retries; `on-first-retry` records one attempt only.

prompt: Why should the step that copies `test-results/` off a build server run whatever the outcome?

choices.text: Because the report is needed to mark the build green
choices.why: The build's status comes from the test command's exit code, not from a copied folder.

choices.text: Because Playwright deletes the folder when it exits
choices.why: Playwright leaves the folder; the machine is what gets thrown away when the job ends.

choices.text: Failed runs are the ones with evidence
choices.why: Right. Evidence is kept for failures, and a success-only step skips exactly those runs.

choices.text: To keep the disk cost down
choices.why: Copying more often costs more disk, not less; the lifetime of the copies is what bounds it.

prompt: A test signs in with a real employee's account and keeps a trace on failure. What is the risk in the artefact?

choices.text: The trace grows too large for the build service to upload
choices.why: A sign-in adds a few requests; size is not the problem here.

choices.text: The trace viewer refuses to open traces that contain cookies
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so; the viewer opens whatever was recorded.

choices.text: The video shows the password as it was typed into the form
choices.why: A password field draws dots on screen; the trace's network lines are where the secret travels.

choices.text: Anyone who opens it reads what the sign-in exchanged
choices.why: Right. A trace holds requests and responses, bodies included, so test accounts should be fake and artefacts private.

prompt: A screenshot test passes on your laptop and fails on the build server on every line of text, with no change to the page. What is the likeliest cause?

choices.text: The baseline was never committed to version control
choices.why: Then the server would have no baseline and would write one and fail with *a snapshot doesn't exist*, not with differing text.

choices.text: The server's fonts draw the text differently
choices.why: Right. Text is drawn by the system's fonts and anti-aliasing, which differ between machines.

choices.text: The server's screen is smaller
choices.why: The browser's window size comes from the configuration, not from a screen, and a build server has none.

choices.text: `toHaveScreenshot` is too slow on servers
choices.why: Slowness would show as a timeout, not as pixels that differ.

prompt: Why did the first run of `evidence/visual.spec.js` fail?

choices.text: There was no baseline yet, so it wrote one
choices.why: Right. *A snapshot doesn't exist … writing actual*; the second run compared against it and passed.

choices.text: The page was still loading its products when the picture was taken
choices.why: The test waits for eight cards before the screenshot; the message names a missing file.

choices.text: The basket still held fruit another test had added
choices.why: The test empties the basket first, for exactly that reason.

choices.text: Screenshots need a headed browser
choices.why: It ran headless and the second run passed.

prompt: A test fails only on the build server, once in twenty runs, and passes on its retry. Which configuration gives you a trace of a failing run?

choices.text: `trace: 'on-first-retry'` with one retry
choices.why: It records the retry, which is the run that passed.

choices.text: `test.fail()` on the test, with any trace setting
choices.why: A failure would then be the expected outcome, and its trace would be deleted like a pass.

choices.text: `trace: 'retain-on-failure'`
choices.why: Right. It records every attempt and keeps the ones whose outcome was not the declared one, the failing first attempt included.

choices.text: `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'`
choices.why: That keeps a picture of the end, not a trace.

prompt: A teammate says the screenshot of a failure *looks fine*, so the test must be wrong. What should you open next?

choices.text: The video, to watch the failure again from the start
choices.why: It would show the same screen arriving; it carries no requests and no times of actions.

choices.text: Nothing; rerun the job until it passes and move on
choices.why: A pass on a later run deletes this run's evidence and explains nothing.

choices.text: The HTML report's index page
choices.why: The report shows the same attachments; the answer is in what the trace holds, wherever you open it.

choices.text: The trace's actions and network
choices.why: Right. A screen that looks fine moves the question to order and time, which only the trace records.

prompt: Which of these did the trace of the failing click hold? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A copy of the video
choices.why: Right. A resource of 106675 bytes, the size of `video.webm`.

choices.text: The start time of the click
choices.why: Right. `"startTime":2191.589` on the click's line.

choices.text: A `POST /api/basket`
choices.why: The network file had three lines and none of them was a POST: the click sent nothing.

choices.text: The shop's own server log for the request
choices.why: A trace is recorded on the browser's side; what the server printed to its own log is not in it.
